text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA /Plc said on Monday that U.S fund manager Northern Cross Investments will vote its 36.66 million shares in support of the company's debt restructuring plan to be put to shareholders on July 10.

"Patrick Ponsolle, executive chairman of the Eurotunnel group, has been informed that the 36.66 million voting rights held by funds managed by Northern Cross Investments will vote in favour of the Eurotunnel board's financial restructuring plan at the next shareholders meeting," the company said in a statement. pnt

French lawyer Sophie L'Helias, head of proxy-holder Franklin Global Investor Services (FGIS), earlier said a shareholder owning around 38 million shares had changed its voting position and would vote for the restructuring plan.
Ponsolle last week identified the shareholder as Northern Cross.

A Eurotunnel spokeswoman said Northern Cross held about three percent of the capital. Ponsolle met a Northern Cross fund manager last Thursday in Boston and explained the details of the restructuring proposals, she added.
A second company spokeswoman said, "This shows that a professional and rational investor who studies the plan can only conclude this is the best possible solution".
Ponsolle has warned that rejection of the restructuring would lead to bankruptcy for Eurotunnel.
